subject: RFP: Commercial response — indexed tier pricing & pro-rata graceband
messages:
From: Polaris Health Procurement <procurement@polarishealth.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter.consultant@example.com>
Date: 2026-09-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFP follow-up — commercial clarifications requested

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the initial submission. A couple of clarifications from our commercial team on section C:

1) You listed tiered token rates but also referenced an "indexed tier" in the notes. Can you explain how the indexed price moves relative to our committed baseline?
2) We would like a pro-rata graceband for the first 90 days after go-live to account for ramping traffic. Is that something Redwood can accept and how does it affect overage invoicing?
3) For multi-year commitments, how do you handle annual CPI or list price escalators?

Please attach a clean pricing sheet showing (a) base commit, (b) tier breakpoints, (c) overage formula, and (d) sample invoice calculation.

Anya Petrov
Head of Procurement — Polaris Health
procurement@polarishealth.com

Attachments: Polaris_RFP_SectionC_Commercial.pdf

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Polaris Health Procurement <procurement@polarishealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-07T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up — commercial clarifications requested

Hi Anya — appreciate the clear list. Please find answers below and an attached pricing workbook. Key points up front: we can support an indexed tier that pegs overage bands to a negotiated baseline price (annualized) with a 90-day pro-rata graceband for initial ramp, and we offer a limited CPI cap for multi-year deals.

Summary (see attached RI_Pricing_Sheet_v1.xlsx for line-item math):
- Baseline commit: 200M tokens / month (generation tokens) at $0.0045 per 1k tokens
- Tiered breaks (post-commit incremental pricing):
  - Tier A (0–25% over commit): $0.0050 per 1k
  - Tier B (25–100% over commit): $0.0065 per 1k
  - Tier C (>100% over commit): $0.0090 per 1k
- Indexed tier option: customer may elect to peg overage pricing to an agreed baseline index (our Retail Index or an agreed CPI proxy). If pegged, overage rates adjust annually on the contract anniversary by the index (capped at +5% and floored at -2%).
- 90-day pro-rata graceband: for the first 90 days post-launch we will apply a pro-rata adjustment where overages incurred below 50% of the committed run-rate are billed at 50% of the applicable overage rate (effectively a temporary 50% off on small unexpected ramps). After 90 days, normal invoicing resumes. Graceband applies only once per customer and cannot be stacked with promotional credits.
- Multi-year escalators: by default an annual escalation equal to lesser of CPI or 3% applies to list rates; customers can negotiate a fixed escalator in the signed SOW.
- True-up cadence: quarterly true-ups with netting (credits applied against next invoice). Unused commit credits expire at the end of the contract year unless a rollover is purchased.

Invoice example (from workbook): monthly invoice shows committed charges (flat), then overage tiers calculated against actual usage buckets, then graceband adjustment line if within first 90 days.

We included a sample clause for the SOW and a worked example. Let me know if you want the indexed peg to reference CPI-U or an alternative index; we can also do a fixed-dollar escalator for budgeting simplicity.

Best,
Neha Kapoor

From: Anya Petrov <anya.petrov@polarishealth.com>

Date: 2026-09-08T10:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up — commercial clarifications requested

Neha — this is helpful, thanks. A couple of follow-ups:

- Can you confirm whether the 90-day graceband is refundable credit or a billing-time discount? We prefer invoice credits for audit visibility.
- For the indexed peg, Polaris prefers CPI-U but would accept an agreed healthcare-specific index if Redwood can propose one.
- We need an authorization threshold for discounts >20% to route to executive approval. If you are offering promotional credits or early-term concessions, indicate approval limits.

Also, please confirm whether the Tier A rate applies to incremental tokens within the first 25% over the commit only (i.e., marginal pricing) or if you apply a blended uplift once usage crosses that bucket. Our accounting needs a straightforward marginal calculation.

Thanks — aim to finalize the commercial appendix by 2026-09-14.

Anya

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-09T15:24:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: RFP follow-up — commercial clarifications requested (internal approval)

Neha / Dylan — looping to confirm negotiation levers and approval thresholds. Proposed responses to Anya:

1) 90-day graceband: treat as invoice credit (not cash refund). Issue as an "Onboarding Credit" line item applied in the first monthly invoice that follows the ramp period; legal to review language in SOW.
2) Tier pricing: confirm marginal (incremental per-token) pricing — do not apply blended buckets. Update pricing workbook to show marginal calculation.
3) Index: allow CPI-U by default; offer healthcare index as an optional clause if Polaris provides the benchmark source.
4) Discounts: I can approve up to 15% promotional credits (on committed charges) without exec sign-off. Anything >15% requires director+ approval; >25% requires CRO approval. Put that in the response.

Dylan: please update the RI_Pricing_Sheet_v1.xlsx with marginal math and add a sample invoice line that shows the onboarding credit as a separate negative line. Connor: please send to legal for a quick review of the SOW clause by EOD tomorrow.

Marissa Cole
VP, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
